metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets New Zealand

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results for New Zealand using the PISA 2022 database. The factsheet does not specify whether student sampling weights and replicate weights were applied in the production of the reported estimates, nor does it name any weight variables. For PISA analyses, analysts should use the official PISA sampling weights and replicate weights (when available) to account for the complex two-stage sampling of students within schools and the stratified design across participating countries/economies. The factsheet also reports results based on PISA scaling and uncertainty intervals (95% confidence intervals), indicating that standard PISA variance estimation procedures were used, but the exact weighting/replication implementation is not documented in the provided text.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a PISA 2022 results factsheet that reports proficiency levels, score differences, correlations, and variance explained, rather than providing an ML model that requires explicit plausible-value (PV) handling or a documented missing-data strategy. The outcomes shown are derived from PISA’s established scaling and reporting procedures, but the factsheet text does not describe PV generation/combining rules or any missing-data imputation/deletion method. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling details are not reported in the provided excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the New Zealand analytic sample as 4,682 students in 169 schools who completed the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment (and are described as completing the assessment in mathematics, reading or science as part of the PISA 2022 design). No additional inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., grade restrictions beyond the 15-year-old target, missing-case exclusions, or task-completion filters) are specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD factsheet summarizes PISA 2022 Creative Thinking results for New Zealand among 15-year-old students. PISA 2022 Creative Thinking was administered as a cognitive test with 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). New Zealand’s mean creative thinking score is 36 out of 60, which is significantly higher than the OECD average (33). The factsheet also reports that 87% of students reach at least Level 3, and 40% are top performers (Levels 5–6). It further describes performance gaps by socio-economic status (11.7 score points between top and bottom quartiles) and gender (girls +3.3 points), and links creative thinking to mathematics and reading performance via reported correlations and variance explained. The document notes special PISA implementation conditions (COVID-19 delays and sampling-standard caveats for some economies), but it does not provide an ML modeling pipeline or explicit PV/missing-data handling details in the excerpt.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet rather than an empirical ML study. As such, there is no student-level predictive modeling, no ML algorithm comparison, and no target-variable-specific performance metrics (e.g., AUC/RMSE) to extract into main_findings. The factsheet also does not document PV combining rules or missing-data handling procedures in the provided text, because it relies on PISA’s standard scaling and reporting pipeline.
